## Background

This Streamlit app was made in **March 2025** as part of my final semester for the [Industry Experience Studio Project](https://handbook.monash.edu/2025/units/FIT5120) unit. The repo is no longer maintained, and the live air quality API it relies on may have changed since, so some pages may need updating. 

A live demo can be found [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R_QbQq_jegXa2rwZfxTAKyIh8cVFW5TT/view?usp=sharing){target="_blank"} along with the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/mary-emm/nafas/tree/main/nafas/onboarding){target="_blank"}.

This was also my first attempt at web development (while only on Python), and there were a lot of things I would have done differently. But I was proud of this mostly.

## Aim

The target audience was Malaysian parents of children with asthma, in line with [SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being](https://globalgoals.org/goals/3-good-health-and-well-being/){target="_blank"}. The app has four parts:

* **Real-time monitor:** current AQI, temperature, humidity and pollutant levels (PM2.5, PM10, O₃) for 40 stations, pulled from the WAQI API, with child-specific guidance.
* **Learn:** a guide to childhood asthma, plus charts comparing yearly state-level AQI with national childhood asthma cases (IHME data, stored in SQLite).
* **Travel:** pick an origin, destination and date, and get a forecast AQI and a 5-day outlook for the destination city. Models were pickled and stored [here](https://github.com/mary-emm/nafas/tree/main/nafas/onboarding/All_States){target="_blank"}.
* **Assess:** combines live AQI and PM2.5 with the child's asthma severity to give an outdoor-activity recommendation.

## Data and modelling

Historical air quality data was the hardest part. At the time, I couldn't find a single open source of historical AQI for Malaysia, and the live APIs only returned current readings, so I aggregated daily readings from the [api-malaysia](https://github.com/ynshung/api-malaysia){target="_blank"} repository into a per-city dataset. I then fitted one [Prophet](https://github.com/facebook/prophet){target="_blank"} time-series model per city (that were available), saved each as a pickle file, and loaded them in the app to forecast AQI for the chosen date.

The forecasts are a proof of concept. Because of time constraints, the models were not rigorously validated, and accuracy drops the further the chosen date is from the training data.

More than anything, this project was my first exposure to how Malaysia could improve on their organization of open-source data.
